📚 DAILY MARKET EDUCATION
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

⚠️ UNDERSTANDING LIQUIDATION RISK
Liquidation happens when your margin balance cannot cover ongoing losses on a leveraged position. The exchange automatically closes your trade to prevent a negative balance. This wipes out your allocated margin completely.
- Real market example: Imagine longing Solana SOL at one hundred dollars with ten times leverage. A ten percent drop to ninety dollars instantly erases your margin. The exchange liquidates your position before you can manually exit.
- Practical tip: Always calculate your exact liquidation price before entering any leveraged trade. Place your stop loss well above that critical price level.
SMART MONEY RULE: Leverage magnifies mistakes, not skill. Lower your leverage to survive market volatility.

🐂🐻 BULL VERSUS BEAR MARKETS
A bull market features rising prices, high optimism, and strong upward momentum over a prolonged period. A bear market brings falling prices, widespread pessimism, and sustained downward pressure. Understanding structural market cycles prevents you from fighting the primary trend.
- Real market example: Ethereum ETH experienced a massive bull run in recent years driven by network upgrades and adoption. Conversely, the subsequent prolonged crypto winter tested investor patience during a harsh bear phase.
- Practical tip: Trend alignment is crucial. Never short a raging bull market or buy every dip blindly in a structural bear market.
PRO TIP: Trade in the direction of the macro trend to dramatically increase your probability of success.

💡 THREE DAILY TRADING TIPS
- Define your entry and exit points before placing any cryptocurrency trade. Never make emotional decisions during high volatility spikes on Bitcoin BTC or altcoins.
- Monitor funding rates on perpetual swaps. Extremely high positive funding often signals an overcrowded long market primed for a sharp correction.
- Keep a detailed trading journal. Review your winning and losing trades weekly to identify recurring psychological mistakes and fix them.

🛡️ MANAGING RISK PER TRADE
Risk management is the only variable you can fully control in trading. Never risk more than one to two percent of your total account balance on a single trade. This mathematical buffer ensures a string of losses will never wipe out your capital.
- Real market example: If you have a ten thousand dollar trading account, risking one percent means losing no more than one hundred dollars if your stop loss triggers on an Avalanche AVAX trade.
- Practical tip: Size your position based on the distance to your stop loss, not based on how much profit you hope to make.
PRO TIP: Preserving capital during drawdowns is far more important than chasing aggressive short-term gains.
